title: Runa's Wonderful Discoveries
markdown:
Runa the rabbit loved her boat, the Whispering Willow, the way some rabbits love a favourite burrow that happens to float. On sunny mornings she steered it gently along Willow Creek, whiskers wiggling with quiet joy. She loved showing friends the lovely things along the water, giving each sight a name as if a name were a gift. “And now,” she would whisper, voice like rustling leaves, “we shall see the marvelous moss patch.” Little mice and mellow hedgehogs leaned forward, eyes wide, at the soft green that really was only moss and, in her voice, a kingdom.

Theo the crow, feathers like dark velvet, watched with a fond caw. He understood the gentle showing. “More than moss. A green kingdom for tiny beetles.” Runa giggled. “Every little wonder deserves a whole heart.”

Her way spread. Aunt Fern, a wise badger, joined one quiet afternoon. “The old willow tree. Branches like sleepy arms for the moon.” Aunt Fern’s smile was slow and warm.

They drifted past smooth pebbles. “The glistening gemstones of the creek bed. Each one a treasure.” Aunt Fern chuckled, honey-voiced. “Such simple beauty you always show us.”

The next Saturday the boat was fuller: cheerful voles, a hedgehog who had come back for the moss, and Professor Hoot, who liked rivers when they did not require flying. As Runa pointed to a water lily with her usual care, a young vole named Pip gasped, copying the flourish exactly. “Oh, Mummy! Look! The fluffy cloud!” He pointed not at the sky but at his mother’s soft ear. The mother giggled, a sound like little bells that the creek decided to keep.

Theo offered a knowing caw. Professor Hoot murmured, “A fluffy ear. Remarkable.”

Runa watched Pip’s joyful pointing. A smile. It was not the same as a lily. It was sweetly its own thing.

Aunt Fern, who had come to meet them, walked over. “Your way of showing is special. You make us see wonder. And Pip has a talent too. Sometimes a fluffy ear is the most delightful thing to point at.”

“It is fluffy!” Pip agreed.

Runa felt a warm glow. She looked at the ear, then, with a gentle flourish, pointed. “The most delightful fluffy ear in all of Willow Creek.” Soft contented laughter.

As the sun dipped low, painting the sky in soft twilight hues, she brought the Whispering Willow to its resting place. Passengers disembarked with contented smiles, the hedgehog promising to return for the moss. Theo landed softly on the thwart. “A perfect day, Runa.”

Aunt Fern offered warm chamomile, steam like a small second creek. “Sometimes the most extra things are closest to us. You remind us to look, and to see what is already there.”

Runa sipped, warmth in the cup and the chest. Water reflected the twilight and the first shy stars. The showing, the borrowed showing, the fluffy-ear showing — all peaceful. The creek kept its own quiet sound, a soft lullaby nobody had to name. She did not ask anyone to settle. She logged moss / sleepy willow / Pip’s ear in a damp-edged notebook, left Theo a crumb on the thwart, and let Aunt Fern pour a second cup while the Whispering Willow bumped the bank like a boat that had finished pointing for the day and was ready, if asked, to point again tomorrow.
